### Must Fix (conclusion-changing only)

1. **DV-3 null is not matched to the max-over-singular-vectors statistic it tests against.** The DV-3 OBSERVED value is `max_i cos(b_down, u_i^base[down_proj])` — a maximum over ~3584 base singular vectors per layer, then max over the L20–L27 band (~28k cosines). The null is specified (§5 line 187, §0 line 21, §2 line 52) only as a "frequency-matched random-singular-vector null (200 draws, matched norm)" with the H-intruder prediction phrased as "≈ frequency-matched null **floor**". Nowhere does the plan state that the max-over-i (over the SAME singular-vector set + band) is applied INSIDE each null draw. A max of ~28k cosines is an extreme-value statistic: even a genuinely random intruder write sits far above the single-direction random floor `1/√3584=0.0167` (the value the word "floor" implies) and far above a flat p95 of 200 single cosines. So with the null as written, a true intruder direction reads "peak above null" by construction → a FALSE H-pre-existing verdict on the headline discriminator. Why conclusion-changing: DV-3 IS the headline ("intruder vs pre-existing"); §7 falsifies H-ungated/intruder if "DV-3 shows a clear peak above null on either behavior." A mismatched null guarantees that clear peak regardless of mechanism, flipping the headline claim. → Fix: define the DV-3 null as the **max-matched order statistic** — for each of B random unit-vector draws `b̃` (norm-matched), compute `max_i cos(b̃, u_i^base)` over the identical ~3584 down_proj singular vectors AND max over the same L20–L27 band, then report p95 over that null max-distribution (and likewise `max_j cos(ã, v_j^base)` for the read arm).
